Thanks for the heads up and for sharing the logs. We're already investigating and will provide a concise executive summary plus the full postmortem and action-item rollup ahead of your QBR.

Preliminary notes:

- Fallback routing to smaller-sequence model variants limited customer-facing impact but did increase cost and degraded quality for some sessions.

Markus will lead the technical postmortem and include mitigations and timeline. Hannah will own the operational follow-ups (runbooks, SLO verification, canary thresholds). Evelyn will align SLA wording for any QBR slides.

Team / Laura —

Attached is the draft postmortem (redwood_postmortem_20260221.pdf) and an exported log bundle (jira-SUP-7781-log-export.tar.gz). Highlights:

Root cause (short): concurrent GC + kernel scheduling jitter on older instance families led to a buildup of inference queue depth for certain sequence-length distributions; our dynamic batching heuristic misclassified some requests leading to inefficient kernel selection under load.

Impact: ~0.6% of customer sessions saw >5s tail p99 latency increases for chat endpoints; embedding throughput degraded for ~45 minutes in two regions.

Mitigations (implemented):
- Hotfix: adjusted batching timeout thresholds + forced kernel re-selection path for sequences >2048 tokens (deployed Feb 21 03:40 UTC).
- Fallback routing: auto-failover to the lighter quantized model variant for impacted capacity (enabled).

Planned follow-ups (owners & ETA):
1) Replace older instance families in pool with refreshed images + kernel patches — owner: MarkUs_Kline (markus_klein) — ETA: 3 weeks.
2) Batching heuristic rewrite with workload-aware thresholds + unit tests — owner: Hannah Schmitt — ETA: 4 weeks.
3) Canary config for kernel-selection changes with telemetry dashboards — owner: Evelyn Hart — ETA: 2 weeks.
4) SLA verification sweep & customer-facing executive note for QBR — owner: Rishi Malhotra — ETA: 5 business days.

I've added inline logs and a short reproducer in the PDF. Laura, let me know if you want any additional telemetry slices for Acme-specific sessions.

Attachments: redwood_postmortem_20260221.pdf (PDF, 450KB), jira-SUP-7781-log-export.tar.gz (tar.gz, 12MB)

-Markus

Subject: Executive summary + QBR slide pack: Feb tail-latency incident & action rollup

Laura —

Attached are the executive summary (below) and the QBR slide pack (qbr_exec_slide_reliability_v2.pptx). This version is tailored to highlight impact, mitigations, and concrete timelines for the actions we will present during the QBR.

Executive summary (for slides):
- Incident window: 2026-02-20 02:13–02:46 UTC. Tail-latency spike for chat & embedding endpoints in us-west-2 and us-east-1.
- Root cause: interaction between GC pressure on legacy worker instances and kernel-selection heuristics in our batcher for long sequences.
- Customer impact: ~0.6% of sessions; Acme saw fallback routing for a subset leading to degraded answer quality for ~8% of affected sessions.
- Immediate actions taken: hotfix to batching timeouts, enabled fallback to quantized model variant, emergency instance replacement queue prioritized.
- Next steps / timeline: replace affected instances (3w), batching rewrite (4w), canary + dashboards (2w), SLA verification and QBR language (5bd).
- Proposed customer remediation: guideline for a one-time bill credit rule for sessions with >2 minutes of degraded quality; recommended credit range: 5–10% on affected usage (to be confirmed with billing).

Action items (who & when):
- Markus: instance replacement plan + weekly status updates (weekly)
- Hannah: batching rewrite PRs + test coverage (4w)
- Evelyn: dashboards + SLA language (2w)
- Rishi: QBR slide delivery + customer remediation proposal (today)

Laura — please find the slide deck attached and a link to the full postmortem and logs here: https://drive.reddemo.com/file/d/1aB2cQ_postmortem. Happy to walk through these slides before the QBR; suggest a 30-minute dry run on Wed.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
